highlights:

# Spot GPU Pricing: How to Get H100 at $0.99/hr (2026 Guide)

 📅 July 29, 2026 📖 8 min read 🏷️ GPU Pricing, H100, Spot Instances, Cloud Cost 

If you're training or inferencing on NVIDIA H100 GPUs in 2026, the difference between spot and on-demand pricing is the single biggest lever you have to control costs. We're talking $0.99/hr vs $8.50/hr for the same hardware — an 88% savings that can mean the difference between a viable startup and a burned-through runway.

This guide breaks down exactly what spot GPU pricing is, which providers offer the best rates right now, and how to build a workload strategy that maximises savings without sacrificing reliability.

 ⚡ Bottom line: Vast.ai and Spheron both offer H100 spot at $0.99/hr — the lowest in the market. Compare that to AWS on-demand at $8.50/hr and the choice is clear: spot pricing is the smart play for non-critical workloads in 2026.

...

## H100 Spot vs On-Demand: Full Pricing Table (July 2026)

We pulled real-time pricing from Parallel API and provider dashboards. All prices are per hour for a single NVIDIA H100 (80GB).

| Provider | Spot | On-Demand | Savings | Interrupt Risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vast.ai | $0.99 | $2.50 | 60% | Medium |
| Spheron | $0.99 | $2.50 | 60% | Medium |
| Nebius | $1.80 | $3.20 | 44% | Low |
| CoreWeave | $2.10 | $3.30 | 36% | Low |
| Lambda | $2.40 | $3.80 | 37% | Low |
| AWS (p3.2xlarge) | $5.00 | $8.50 | 41% | High |

Prices captured July 29, 2026 via Parallel API and direct provider listings. Spot prices fluctuate — check live data before provisioning.

...

### 🥇 Vast.ai & Spheron — $0.99/hr (Best Value)

Both marketplace-style platforms aggregate individual GPU owners alongside datacenter capacity. This creates a deep pool of spot inventory that keeps prices competitive. Vast.ai has the broadest selection (H100, A100, A6000, RTX 4090), while Spheron focuses on a curated set of verified hosts. At $0.99/hr for H100 spot, they're the cheapest options by a wide margin. The catch: interrupt frequency is higher, so you must implement checkpointing. Use their Python SDKs or Docker-based workflows for seamless resumption.

...

The smartest strategy? Hybrid provisioning. Run training on spot (Vast.ai or Spheron at $0.99/hr), keep production inference on on-demand (CoreWeave at $3.30/hr), and overflow to AWS on-demand ($8.50/hr) only when all other capacity is exhausted.

...

## The 2026 Spot Market Outlook

Three trends are shaping spot GPU pricing for the rest of 2026:

1. More supply, but more demand. NVIDIA shipped more H100s in Q2 2026 than any previous quarter, but Blackwell B200 allocations are eating into H100 supply. Expect spot prices to stay flat through Q3 and rise 10-15% in Q4 as the Blackwell transition accelerates.

2. Marketplace providers are gaining share. Vast.ai and Spheron have grown their H100 fleets by 3x since January. More supply means more competitive pricing — the $0.99 floor may hold through year-end.

3. Hyperscaler spot is becoming less attractive. AWS spot on H100 went from $3.50 to $5.00 in 2026 as the big cloud providers reprioritise on-demand margin. The gap between hyperscaler spot and marketplace spot has never been wider.

 🎯 The takeaway: The spot window has never been better for H100. $0.99/hr is historically low. Lock in multi-month spot reservations where providers offer them, and budget for a 15-20% spot price increase in Q4 2026.

results.title: H100 Cloud Pricing 2026: Hourly Rates by Provider
results.author: CloudGpu Team
highlights:
## H100 Cloud Pricing 2026: Hourly Rates by Provider

NVIDIA H100 cloud rental costs roughly $1.99/hr on RunPod, $2.49/hr on Lambda Labs, and about $1.87/hr on Vast.ai, dropping to ~$1.03/hr on spot (Spheron). Hyperscalers charge far more — up to ~$12/hr on Azure. The most striking fact about H100 pricing in 2026: the same GPU can cost nearly 14x more on one provider than another.

...

## H100 pricing by provider

Rates below are single-GPU H100 hourly prices as of mid-2026. Note that SXM and PCIe variants differ, and spot prices fluctuate constantly.

| Provider | Type | On-demand ($/hr) | Spot ($/hr) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spheron | Neo-cloud / marketplace | ~$2.50 | ~$1.03 |
| RunPod | Specialized | $1.99 (Community) / $2.89 (Secure) | ~$1.19 |
| Vast.ai | Marketplace (P2P) | ~$1.49–$1.87 | lower, varies |
| Cudo Compute | Neo-cloud | ~$1.80 | — |
| TensorDock | Marketplace | ~$1.99–$2.25 | — |
| Lambda Labs | Specialized | $2.49–$2.99 (SXM), $3.29 (PCIe) | — |
| CoreWeave | Enterprise neo-cloud | ~$6.16 | + spot |
| AWS (p5) | Hyperscaler | ~$6.88 | ~$2.00–$2.50 |
| GCP (a3) | Hyperscaler | ~$3.00–$11.06 | — |
| Azure | Hyperscaler | ~$12.29 | — |

> ⚠️ H100 spot prices can change multiple times per hour. Every figure here is a snapshot — verify live rates before renting.

The takeaway is clear: neo-clouds and marketplaces cluster around $1.50–$3.00/hr, while hyperscalers run 2–5x higher for the identical GPU. If you don’t need enterprise compliance, paying hyperscaler rates for an H100 is usually overpaying.

...

A community thread tracking H100 rates across 25 providers found a 13.8x price difference for the same GPU — from $0.80/hr at the cheapest to over $11/hr at the most expensive. That gap comes down to four factors:

Provider tier. Marketplaces pool spare capacity and compete on price; specialized neo-clouds add reliability at a modest premium; hyperscalers charge most for compliance and integration.

Billing model. Spot/interruptible rates undercut on-demand by 50–80%. The Spheron spot floor of ~$1.03/hr versus its $2.50/hr on-demand shows the size of that discount.

GPU variant. The H100 SXM (higher bandwidth, NVLink) and H100 PCIe are priced differently — and how a provider publishes the price matters too. Hyperscalers often quote a full VM (compute, memory, storage bundled), which inflates the headline number versus a “naked GPU” rate.

Region and availability. Capacity-constrained regions cost more, and prices shift as supply changes.

## How H100 prices have fallen

H100 rental has become dramatically cheaper since its 2023 launch. Early adopters paid rates like $7–11/hr on hyperscalers; by 2026 specialist clouds routinely offer the same GPU under $3/hr. The arrival of the B200 (Blackwell) is pushing H100 prices down further as data centers upgrade and demand shifts to newer silicon. If you’re renting H100s, this trend works in your favor — but it also means any quoted price ages quickly.

...

### What’s the cheapest H100?

 Spot pricing on marketplaces and neo-clouds is cheapest — around $1.03/hr on Spheron spot as of mid-2026, with RunPod spot occasionally near $1.19/hr. The trade-off is interruptibility, so use checkpointing.

highlights:
Newer silicon is not always the smarter buy.

$4.96/hr and $5.85/hr. Two GPUs, one generation apart, less than a dollar between them per hour. The cheaper option is last year's chip, and it might still be the right call for your workload.

Current Spheron marketplace pricing, subject to availability and may vary by region:

$4.96/hr is on-demand H200, with spot as low as $3.31/hr (33% off).

$5.85/hr is on-demand B300, the lowest bookable on-demand rate on the whole marketplace.

Here's how to choose:

Pick H200 if you run a proven Hopper-class training or inference pipeline and want the lowest cost per token today. The spot rate alone cuts a third off your bill.

Pick B300 instead if you need current-gen Blackwell Ultra silicon for newer model architectures and want the cheapest on-demand entry point on the platform.

## Restated Aug 7, 2026

Restated from $6.5175 across 4 providers to $5.2225 across 6.

- Crusoe and Lambda were excluded on 2026-07-29 because a single 30-day editorial-review clock had lapsed, even though the collector was re-reading and confirming both prices every morning and neither price moved during July. - All six constituents were re-verified live on 2026-08-07 and every price reconciled unchanged. The eligibility gate now runs separate clocks for automated price checks and editorial review.
